results.name: Miles Morales - Blender Cycles with Rig
results.description:
This is Miles Morales from the Spiderman into the spider verse Film

I rigged the model in blender using the Rigify addon provided with blender 

Compatible with blender 3.0, 2.93, 2.80, ect

Miles Morales is one of the main protagonists in Marvel's Spider-Man series. He is a prominent supporting character in Marvel's Spider-Man, and the titular protagonist of the standalone expansion Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales. A seventeen-year-old teenager, he is a friend of Peter Parker and the son of police officer Jefferson Davis. Peter befriends Miles after his father's death, introducing him to the non-profit F.E.A.S.T. shelter so he can serve as a volunteer. Miles is unaware of Peter's secret identity as the masked vigilante Spider-Man, whom Miles idolizes. He eventually gains spider-like powers himself, which he reveals to Peter, who in turn reveals being Spider-Man. Under Peter's guidance, Miles attempts to step up as New York City's next superhero.

results.name: Lair of a killer surgeon
results.description:
This is a small scene made for a study project. my goal here was to create an environment that tells a story of a disturbing individual through environmental clues.

In this case a killer surgeon. He kidnaps his victims and drains them of their blood for selling but also for consumption.

I've added annotations to detail a bit more about the environment but the piece is made to stand on its own.

I had a lot of fun and hardship creating this piece, learned a lot and got inspired to do more.
Hopefully you enjoy it too!

All assets are modeled and textured by me, excluding the portraits generated with Thispersondoesnotexist and the free stock photo of the police officer.

results.name: Bad Vibes in NY
results.description:
I used 7 different datasets from the [Open Data of New York](https://opendata.cityofnewyork.us/) to create (in python) this visualization:

* Points of Interest (Top layer in red)
* Office of Emergency Management responses (Orange-ish)
* Graffitis removal (Third "layer", spanning in green)
* 311 service requests (Turquoise)
* Motored vehicle collisions (Bright blue)
* NYPD Complaints calls (Purple)
* NYPD Arrests (Fuchsia)

Each dataset was subdivided into sub-categories, and vertically arranged according to the number of events in this category. 

For instance, the first few layers (top to bottom) for the 311 service requests (turquoise layer) correspond to hot water issues, residential noise, illegal parking, street condition... and one on the bottom (hence less frequent) even matches complaints for illegal animals kept as pets !

As this model is far from meaningful, I'll probably soon try to create some animated visualizations mapping events from specific categories according to time of day for instance.
